extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and recipients (investigators and administrative staff preparing biosketches)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating the NIH biographical sketch (biosketch) attachment required for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors on NIH grant applications and certain progress reports. Covers who must submit, when it is required, and which format/tools to use (including fellowship vs non‑fellowship variants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Purpose of the biosketch
rubrics_metrics.description: A biographical sketch (also referred to as biosketch) documents an individual's qualifications and experience for a specific role in a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH staff and peer reviewers utilize the biosketch to ensure that individuals included on the applications are equipped with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research. Ensure the biosketch clearly demonstrates relevant qualifications for the specific project role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must submit a biosketch
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires submission of a biosketch for each proposed senior/key personnel and other significant contributor on a grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some funding opportunities or programs may also request biosketches for additional personnel (e.g., Participating Faculty Biosketch attachment for institutional training awards). Confirm the specific funding opportunity's instructions to identify all required individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: When biosketches are required (timing/occurrences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and recipients are required to submit biosketches in competing applications for all types of grant programs, in progress reports when new senior/key personnel or other significant contributors are identified, and to support prior approval requests for changes in senior/key personnel status and changes of recipient organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include updated biosketches whenever personnel changes occur that the application or award policies require; use biosketches to support administrative actions (e.g., prior approvals) as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format conformity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH biosketches must conform to a specific format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and recipients can use the provided format pages to prepare their biosketch attachments. Follow the required layout and fields exactly as specified on the format pages; deviations could lead to noncompliance with application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted tools to create/format biosketches (SciENcv and format pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and recipients can use SciENcv, a tool used to develop and automatically format biosketches according to NIH requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SciENcv can automatically format biosketch content to the NIH-required format pages. Alternatively, applicants may use the provided format page templates. Choose the method that ensures conformance with NIH formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the correct biosketch variant (Fellowship vs Non‑Fellowship)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are distinct format pages for Biosketch (Non‑Fellowship) and Biosketch (Fellowship): Biographical Sketch Format Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fellowship-specific biosketch format when preparing applications for fellowship mechanisms; use the non‑fellowship format for other grant applications. Verify which variant the funding opportunity requires before preparing the attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special cases: additional required biosketch attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Some funding opportunities or programs may request biosketches for additional personnel (e.g., Participating Faculty Biosketch attachment for institutional training awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read opportunity-specific instructions to determine if extra attachments are required (such as participating faculty for training awards) and follow the designated format pages for those attachments.
